Carried from round 1 (backup-db.sh@stage-2:7-18; output 'tables in the backup: 7', 'the exit code of the last command was 0'). Round 2 text 'in the pg_dump command' replaces 'line 12' and is correct. Added gloss '0, the number a command returns to say it succeeded' is the standard shell convention; the lesson does not attribute this 0 to pg_dump (in the script $? on line 18 reports the preceding echo).

PostgreSQL 17 pg_dump: "Dumps can be output in script or archive file formats. Script dumps are plain-text files containing the SQL commands required to reconstruct the database"; -F p plain: "Output a plain-text SQL script file (the default)."; -s: "Dump only the object definitions (schema), not data." The new definition states the default script format as what pg_dump always writes.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: `pg_dump` is PostgreSQL's tool that writes a database out as a file, called a dump; by default, as here, the file is plain SQL statements that rebuild the database.

claim_verdicts.evidence: backup-db.sh:4-5 "Everything below runs inside the lab box; this line puts it there." [ -f /.dockerenv ] || exec .../lab-run.sh. docker-compose.yml defines lab (container donhang-lab) and db (donhang-db) as services of one Compose project, i.e. containers on one Docker host. /tmp/backups is not a mounted volume of lab, so the file sits in that container on the same machine.
claim_verdicts.source: examples/don-hang scripts/terminal/backup-db.sh:4-5; docker-compose.yml services lab, db

Round 2 clause '(the init-scripts lines mount setup files, not the data)' matches: that volume is a ConfigMap, the data folder is the emptyDir.

"For a Pod that defines an emptyDir volume, the volume is created when the Pod is assigned to a node. As the name says, the emptyDir volume is initially empty." "When a Pod is removed from a node for any reason, the data in the emptyDir is deleted permanently." Note: "A container crashing does *not* remove a Pod from a node. The data in an emptyDir volume is safe across container crashes."

Docker docs: "When you create a volume, it's stored within a directory on the Docker host." "A volume's contents exist outside the lifecycle of a given container... Using a volume ensures that the data is persisted even if the container using it is removed." docker-compose.yml db service mounts '- db-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data' (working tree line 99).
